entries.postTitle: Outgrowing Old Identities

captions.threads:
1/4 Nobody warns you that success can feel like a costume that stopped fitting somewhere along the way. You're wearing it because you earned it, because people recognize you in it, because it got you here. But somewhere between the achievement and the next morning, the seams started pinching.

2/4 I spent years building an identity around being the guy who had it figured out. Digital marketing veteran, the one with the systems, the frameworks, the answers. It worked until it didn't. The identity wasn't false exactly, but it was incomplete in ways I couldn't articulate. Like wearing someone else's definition of success and calling it mine.

3/4 The weird part is that outgrowing an identity doesn't mean it was wrong. It means you're expanding faster than the container you built. Your nervous system knows before your ego admits it. You start noticing the gap between who you're performing and who you're actually becoming. That gap gets uncomfortable fast.

4/4 The exit isn't a dramatic rebrand or a spiritual awakening post. It's quieter. It's realizing you can hold multiple truths at once, integrate what worked without being trapped by it, and build a new shape that fits your actual life now. The costume comes off because you finally have permission to let it.

https://vibrationofawesome.com/blog/boom/posts/outgrowing-old-identities
